newsitem.title: USA: Eight days of Gulf War logs missing - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Eight days of Gulf War logs missing - NYT.

text.p: Eight days of military logs covering a period when U.S. troops might have been exposed to nerve gas and other Iraqi chemical weapons shortly after the 1991 Gulf War cannot be found despite an exhaustive search, The New York Times said in its Thursday edition.

The logs, which appear to have been removed or lost, were maintained for Gen. H. Norman Schwarzkopf and were supposed to record any incident in which chemical or biological agents had been detected, the story said.

The story reports several gaps in the otherwise meticulous combat logs. The gaps include a period in early March 1991 when U.S. combat engineers blew up the sprawling Kamisiyah ammunition depot in southern Iraq, which may have exposed thousands of U.S. troops to nerve gas, the Times reported.

The logs are considered important evidence by ailing Gulf War veterans who believe their health was damaged by exposure to Iraqi chemical weapons. Portions made public so far show that U.S. commanders disregarded several reports of chemical detections during the war, the story said.

The Defence Department, which at one time had denied to Congress that such combat records existed, released them last year to a Georgia veterans group that sought them under the Freedom of Information Act, the story said.

When the veterans group noted several pages from the logs were missing for key dates, the Pentagon said it would investigate. But the Pentagon on Wednesday said it had not turned up any additional pages that would fill the gaps, the story said.
"We've done what we can do," Lieut. Col. Nino Fabiano, a spokesman for the United States Central Command, is quoted as saying in the story.
